story.title: It grounds your business, then the tree knows it.
story.lead1: SkillTree interviews and skills are one layer. Agent KBase is the company knowledge base those agents read: offers, constraints, voice, and what must stay [CONFIRM].
story.lead2: That is the difference between an AI org that shares ground truth and a folder of generic prompts.
story.step1Body: Run `brain setup` (npm: `@agentkbase/cli`) or open the web wizard. Same pack from CLI and browser.
story.step2Body: Step through Project, Facts, Story, and Gaps. Paste a public URL to draft from the landing page, then edit like an interview transcript.
story.step3Body: Validation passes → export `brain.zip`. Facts, stories, AGENTS.md, and open questions become the node at the center of the tree.
story.step4Body: Cursor loads `brain/` before tasks. SkillTree skills sit on the SKILLS spoke: how to work, while Agent KBase holds what is true.
story.extractTitle: Point it at a site. Watch FACTS and GAPS fill.
story.extractLead: Step 1 of the wizard: paste a public URL. We read titles, headings, and body copy, then draft mission text, fact bullets, and story beats onto the map. Open questions land on GAPS as [CONFIRM] until you approve them.
story.extractMuted: The graph is the same radial layout teams use for audits: scan the public page, plan on spokes, export only after you edit. SkillTree runs paid full stack audits; Agent KBase gives you the OSS map and zip for your repo.
story.synced: Nodes synced from your wizard draft
story.sample: Sample after URL extract · FACTS and GAPS highlighted ·

company.title: The knowledge layer every agent reads
company.lead: Paste your site. Correct the draft until you recognise what you sell, who it is for, and what must not be said. From then on, every agent that speaks for the business reads that same base. A price, a client, or a claim that is not there is cut, or marked for you to confirm. Nothing goes live until you say yes. An article or a LinkedIn post comes after.
company.stepsTitle: From your URL to a base you recognise
company.step1: Paste the public URL in the wizard and extract a draft.
company.step2: Cross out any service, price, or deadline you do not sell.
company.step3: Write who you serve, and what you will not claim.
company.step4: Ask something a client would ask. Every agent has to answer from that base.
company.step5: If you trust the draft, an article or a LinkedIn post can come next. You approve it first.
company.validLine: A line is valid when it is in your files, or marked for you to confirm, or cut.
company.checksLead: Nothing goes live unless every line is yes. A person compares each fact with what you actually sell.
company.check1: The title is a shop or studio problem, not a jargon word.
company.check2: Every price, pack, or deadline is on your site. If it is not, it is cut.
company.check3: No rankings, traffic, or client names you cannot prove.
company.check4: The draft says where each fact came from: your site or a public page.
company.check5: The ask is the waitlist, the site, or the brand WhatsApp. Never invoices, passwords, or a personal phone.
company.firstArticle: First article that used this list:
company.articleTitle: How to stop your blog publishing prices that do not exist
company.core1: OSS stays read-only: facts in git, wizard, CLI, MCP brief and validate
company.core2: WhatsApp queue: draft in, approve or reject out
company.core3: Blog publish only when the article is approved
company.core4: LinkedIn drafts only from a published article
company.coreHint: MCP will not gain write or publish tools. Connectors live outside the public npm MCP. Done-for-you means we operate the loop; you approve on WhatsApp.
company.dfyDesc: We install the base from your public site. You correct it. You approve anything an agent would publish. Setup call, then a written agreement.
company.actDesc: Same three connectors for teams that already keep a brain in git. Ships after the operated loop is proven. Not a Zapier catalogue.
